title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurates Deepotsav 2026 celebrations in Ayodhya
subtitle:
Deepotsav has evolved into a celebration of Jan Bhagidari, reflecting Bharat’s collective faith: Vice-President

Millions of lamps in Ayodhya symbolise transformation in the lives of crores of Indians: Vice-President

India must embrace modern aspirations while remaining rooted in its civilisational values: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 NOV 2026 9:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, inaugurated the Deepotsav 2026 celebrations at Ram Ki Paidi in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, today. He witnessed the spectacular illumination of the ghats with millions of diyas, cultural presentations depicting the Ramayana and musical fireworks. He also participated in the sacred Saryu Aarti at Naya Ghat.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan participated as the Chief Guest in the grand Deepotsav 2026 celebrations at Ram Ki Paidi, Ayodhya, today, witnessing the spectacular illumination of the ghats with millions of diyas. https://t.co/bBGAik7gMs
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 7, 2026
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan performed aarti on the banks of the Saryu in Ayodhya as he participates in Deepotsav 2026 https://t.co/igtgnFjFbZ
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 7, 2026
Addressing the gathering at Ram Ki Paidi, the Vice-President highlighted the remarkable growth of Deepotsav since its inception in 2017, when over 1.7 lakh lamps were illuminated. He said that the celebration reached over 26 lakh lamps in 2025, while its tenth edition envisaged more than 30 lakh diyas at Ram Ki Paidi and over 70 lakh across Ayodhya. He congratulated the Uttar Pradesh Government for taking the festival to national and international prominence.
The Vice-President appreciated the festival’s contribution to local livelihoods, creating opportunities for potters, rural women, artisans, performers, hotel and homestay operators, guides and transport providers. He also welcomed the innovative use of technology, including more than 2,100 indigenous drones depicting scenes from the Ramayana and the participation of around 1,000 artists in cultural programmes.
Referring to the millions of lamps illuminating Ayodhya, he said they symbolised the transformation taking place in the lives of crores of Indians. He appreciated Uttar Pradesh’s initiatives in women’s empowerment, education, agriculture, healthcare, housing and entrepreneurship, and observed that the State was progressing towards becoming ‘Uttam Pradesh’.
Addressing the youth, the Vice-President urged them to understand the Ramayana and imbibe its teachings in their daily conduct. He called upon young people to embrace science, innovation and technology while remaining connected to India’s values, languages, traditions and cultural wisdom. India must be modern in its aspirations while remaining firmly rooted in its civilisational values, he said.
Earlier, the Vice-President offered prayers at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple and participated in special prayers and aarti of Shri Ram-Janaki at Ram Katha Park.

November 7, 2026
Addressing the gathering at Ram Katha Park, the Vice-President said that Bhagwan Shri Ram is the eternal embodiment of Dharma, righteousness, compassion and ideal conduct.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan participated in the special prayers and aarti of Shri Ram-Janaki at Ram Katha Park, Ayodhya, as part of the Deepotsav 2026 celebrations. https://t.co/JTJD3IILZk
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 7, 2026
Describing Ayodhya as a shining example of ‘Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi’, the Vice-President noted that the development of roads, ghats, pilgrimage facilities, accommodation and improved rail and air connectivity had significantly transformed the experience of pilgrims and visitors.
The Vice-President congratulated the Uttar Pradesh Government, the administration, artists, volunteers, artisans and citizens for making the tenth edition of Deepotsav a grand celebration of Jan Bhagidari, reflecting Bharat’s collective faith and devotion.
The celebrations were attended by Governor of Uttar Pradesh Smt. Anandiben Patel, Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya and Shri Brajesh Pathak, Ministers, revered saints and seers, and other distinguished guests.

title: Raksha Mantri reviews infrastructure development along LAC & deployment of advanced military equipment during visit to Trishakti Corps at Sukna
subtitle:
Lauds the Corps’ role in nation building through progress & community welfare initiatives in border areas

Sukna is a vital link in security architecture of Eastern India; Government is committed to strengthening supply chains to ensure availability of essential supplies to soldiers: Shri Rajnath Singh

“Modern warfare extends beyond conventional battles to encompass hybrid warfare, proxy wars, cyber-attacks, drone incursions & information warfare; Defence Forces must remain vigilant”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 NOV 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh reviewed the operational preparedness of Trishakti Corps at Sukna, West Bengal, on November 7, 2026. He was briefed on infrastructure development along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and the deployment of advanced military equipment and emerging technologies to enhance operational capabilities & combat effectiveness. Raksha Mantri expressed satisfaction with the operational preparedness of the Corps and appreciated its contribution to nation-building through infrastructure development and community welfare initiatives in border areas, aimed at strengthening ties with local communities. Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth; General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Eastern Command, Lt Gen VMB Krishnan; and General Officer Commanding, 33 Corps, Lt Gen Man Raj Singh Mann were present on the occasion, along with other senior Army officers.
Later, addressing the soldiers during Barakhana on the eve of Diwali, Raksha Mantri commended their courage, professionalism and unwavering dedication towards safeguarding the nation's frontiers under challenging operational conditions. Underlining the importance of logistics in national security, he described Sukna and its surrounding region as a critical hub for the movement of supplies, weaponry, food, medical provisions and personnel to forward locations. He stated that Sukna serves as a vital link in the security architecture of Eastern India and its geographical sensitivity necessitates round-the-clock operational readiness. He added that the Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, is continuously working to strengthen supply chains and ensure that soldiers deployed at forward locations have access to all essential requirements.
Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that budgetary allocations for roads, tunnels, border infrastructure and modern equipment have been increased, with the nation steadily progressing towards 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat'. “Our start-ups and industries are now manufacturing drones, anti-drone systems, and other state-of-the-art equipment for the soldiers. It is a matter of pride that our Defence Forces are actively embracing emerging technologies, learning drone operations, enhancing their understanding of cyber security, and undergoing training in new methodologies. This transformation will prepare us for the future,” he said.
Highlighting the changing nature of modern warfare, Raksha Mantri emphasised that security challenges are no longer confined to conventional exchanges of gunfire or artillery along the borders, but encompass hybrid warfare, proxy wars, cyber-attacks, drone incursions and information warfare. He stated that adversaries increasingly resort to spreading rumours through social media, monitoring sensitive locations using drones and attempting to compromise military systems through cyber-attacks. He exhorted the personnel to remain vigilant and prepared to safeguard national security across all domains.
Shri Rajnath Singh reaffirmed the Government's commitment to taking every possible step to boost troop morale and urged officers to spend quality time with soldiers whenever possible. Such interactions, he said, would foster a strong sense of belonging among personnel and reinforce their confidence that the Government and the entire nation stand firmly with them.
Raksha Mantri also underscored the importance of mental health and emotional well-being among Defence Forces personnel. Acknowledging that soldiers may experience stress due to separation from their families and the demands of their duties, he encouraged them to communicate openly with their comrades and seek support rather than suppress their feelings.
Describing the North-Eastern region as the 'first edge' rather than the 'last edge' of India, Shri Rajnath Singh said that the region represents the beginning of the nation's geographical and cultural landscape, as it receives the first rays of the morning sun. He highlighted the North-East's rich biodiversity, natural beauty, cultural diversity and unique traditions, describing it as an integral part of India's identity.
Raksha Mantri extended Diwali greetings to the personnel and their families, assuring them that the Government remains committed to their safety, dignity and well-being. He described Barakhana as a reflection of the spirit of togetherness and equality, stating that such gatherings transcend ranks and hierarchies, bringing personnel from diverse regions, cultures and linguistic backgrounds together as one family.

title: Defence Forces must maintain highest level of operational readiness, with focus on domain awareness, cyber resilience & information integrity to counter emerging threats: Raksha Mantri at Air Force Station, Bagdogra
subtitle:
“Air Warriors deployed at Bagdogra serve as a robust shield for security of eastern sector”

‘Second Tour of Duty’ is a significant Diwali gift for Agniveers, says Shri Rajnath Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 NOV 2026 1:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Defence Forces to maintain the highest level of operational readiness, with special focus on strengthening domain awareness, cyber resilience and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats. Interacting with the personnel of the Indian Air Force (IAF) on the eve of Diwali at Air Force Station, Bagdogra, West Bengal, on November 7, 2026, he emphasised that the security landscape has become increasingly complex, with warfare extending beyond conventional engagements along the borders to encompass asymmetric warfare, proxy wars, cyber-attacks, drone swarms, information operations and narrative management.
“Often, the adversary avoids direct confrontation and instead seeks to exploit our vulnerabilities. Through social media, the adversary may attempt to sow doubt in the minds of the local population and our soldiers by spreading misleading information. In such a scenario, your role extends beyond that of an ordinary soldier,” said Raksha Mantri.
Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important region and a crucial link in India's security framework, particularly for the North-Eastern region, Shri Rajnath Singh commended the courage and dedication of the defence forces personnel towards safeguarding national interests. He stated that the Air Warriors deployed in the region serve as a robust shield for the security of the eastern sector, and their preparedness is fundamental to maintaining stability in the region.
Raksha Mantri underscored that discipline and courage remain indispensable, irrespective of technological advancements, stating that the conduct, bearing, language and restraint of the Defence Forces personnel shape the image of the military among local communities. Lauding the soldiers for discharging their duties with these qualities, he urged them to strengthen their engagement with the local population, particularly in and around Bagdogra, and nurture the deep bond of trust and affection between the people and the Defence Forces. “The more you engage with the local community, the weaker the adversary’s conspiracies will become,” he said.
Reaffirming the Government's resolve to achieve ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’, Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the growing contribution of Indian start-ups and industries in developing drones, anti-drone systems and advanced military equipment. He appreciated the defence forces for embracing indigenous technologies and acquiring new skills in drone operations and cyber security. He underlined the importance of making the military increasingly technology-driven to effectively address future security challenges.
Referring to the Cabinet’s approval of the 'Second Tour of Duty' for Agniveers, Raksha Mantri stated that the decision would provide Agniveers with another opportunity to serve the nation. He added that upon completion of the two-year engagement period, all Agniveers will get an opportunity to be enrolled as regular soldiers subject to their willingness and their meeting selection criteria. He termed the decision as a significant Diwali gift for Agniveers, reiterating the Government's commitment to the welfare of the Defence Forces personnel and their families.
Shri Rajnath Singh extended his Diwali greetings and wished the Air Warriors and their families good health, happiness and prosperity. He said that the personnel, despite missing their families during the festival, remain steadfast in ensuring the security of their fellow citizens. He expressed gratitude to their families for their sacrifices and contributions. He emphasised that while the soldiers remain committed towards safeguarding the borders, the nation will always stand by their families and ensure their well-being.
Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit; Air Officer Commanding, Air Force Station, Bagdogra Air Commodore Manish Sharma; and other senior officials of the IAF were present on the occasion.

title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah reviews Gujarat’s law and order and internal security situation at a high-level meeting in Ahmedabad
subtitle:
Home Minister directs strengthening of border and coastal security, action against drug networks and effective control of cybercrime

Emphasises strengthening surveillance along Gujarat’s nearly 2,340-km-long coastline and better coordination among BSF, State Police, Coast Guard and central agencies

Gujarat’s performance in implementation of new criminal laws commendable; 92 per cent of chargesheets filed within 60 days and 86 per cent within 90 days

Stresses action against entire drug networks and their kingpins, rather than just small-time peddlers, and prioritising financial investigations to seize illicit assets

Directs enhancing the capacity of S4C and the 1930 helpline, strengthening counter-terrorism agencies, and expediting identification and deportation of illegal foreign nationals as per law

Home Minister reiterates commitment to building a secure India through a safe, developed and drug-free Gujarat
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 NOV 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today reviewed the law and order and internal security situation in Gujarat at a high-level meeting in Ahmedabad.
Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendra Patel, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghavi, Union Home Secretary, senior officials of the Ministry of Home Affairs and its subordinate offices, and officials of the State Home Department and other concerned departments attended the meeting.
Several important issues, including border and coastal security, implementation of the new criminal laws, drug trafficking, cybercrime, terrorism, illegal migration and disaster management, were discussed during the meeting.
Keeping in view Gujarat’s nearly 2,340-kilometre-long coastline and its international border with Pakistan, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah emphasised the need to strengthen border and coastal surveillance and ensure better coordination among the Border Security Force (BSF), State Police, Coast Guard and central agencies.
Shri Amit Shah appreciated Gujarat’s performance in the implementation of the new criminal laws, stating that 92 per cent of chargesheets in the state were filed within 60 days and 86 per cent within 90 days. The Home Minister directed the state to launch a special drive to clear more than 25,000 pending forensic cases.
The Union Home Minister said that action against drug trafficking must not remain confined to small-time peddlers. Instead, the entire drug network and its principal kingpins must be targeted, with financial investigations being prioritised to seize their illicit assets.
Shri Amit Shah directed that the capacity of S4C and the 1930 helpline be enhanced to tackle cybercrime, counter-terrorism agencies be strengthened, and the identification and deportation of illegal foreign nationals be expedited in accordance with the law. He appreciated the deportation of 2,412 illegal foreign nationals under special drives.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also emphasised the need to accelerate work relating to disaster management, fire safety, the Ahmedabad Urban Flood Management Project, and the survey and disposal of enemy properties.
At the conclusion of the meeting, the Union Home Minister directed all Central and State agencies to work in close coordination and regularly review progress against prescribed targets. He reiterated the commitment to building a secure India through a safe, developed and drug-free Gujarat.

title: EPFO successfully concludes Special Campaign 6
subtitle: Successful public grievance disposal, cleanliness drives and record management by EPFO meeting all targets set
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 NOV 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Employees’ Provident Fund Organization (EPFO) has successfully concluded the Special Campaign 6 conducted during the month of October 2026, reaffirming its commitment to administrative efficiency, cleanliness, transparency and improved public service delivery. The campaign was made successful by active participation of EPFO Head Office, Training Academies, 21 Zonal Offices and various Regional and District offices. The key achievements on various parameters are as under:
Disposal of public grievances (PG): EPFO disposed 2,36,021 grievances against a target of 2,05,000 (15.1% above target). This includes disposal of 2,02,984 grievances on EPFiGMS against a target of 1,80,000 (12.8% above target) and 33,037 grievances on CPGRAM (32.1% above target).
Disposal of appeals and PMOPG:
Similarly, 10,343 CPGRAM Appeals were disposed of against a target of 5,758, (88.1% above target)
,
while 758 PMOPG were disposed of against a target of 747 (5.1% above target). Target to dispose off 36 VIP references and 2 Parliamentary Assurances was also achieved.
Conduct of Cleanliness Drives: 598 Cleanliness Target Units were identified and transformed successfully against a target of 570, which is 5% above the target. Besides this, drive of beautification of offices, tree plantation and Blood Donation Camp were also conducted during the Campaign. Further, a total of 68,178 sq. ft space has been freed against a target of 28,300 sq. ft (140.1% above target).
Record management: A total of 41,875 physical files have been reviewed against a target of 28,770 (45.6% above target), and 1.383 files have been transferred to the National Archives against a target of 1,277 (8.3% above target). 517 physical files have been identified for weeding against a target of 109 while 342 files have been weeded against the target of 82. As regards e-files, 8,355 e-files have been reviewed against a target of 8,160 (2.4% above target) and 3,106 e-files closed against the target of 3,000 (3.5% above target).
The campaign’s progress was regularly monitored at various levels within the EPFO. Mass pledge-taking activities and other grievance redressal drives were conducted at various offices of EPFO. While redressal of public grievances is an on-going activity, quality disposal of grievances in a time-bound manner was undertaken during the Campaign period. As regards PMOPG, telephonic feedback was taken from the petitioners after its disposal, and an overwhelming percentage of such petitioners expressed satisfaction on the disposal. Furthermore, any suggestions for improvement were also obtained for effecting any micro-level systemic changes.
The activities pertaining to cleanliness and record management have not only made offices clean for public dealing but also created space for efficient office management.
The successful conclusion of Special Campaign 6 reflects the EPFO’S continued commitment to good governance, efficient administration, employee well-being and citizen-centric service delivery.

title: Legislative Department Initiates Interaction Series; First Session Focuses on Improving Values and Personal Effectiveness in Leadership
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 NOV 2026 11:45AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, has initiated an Interaction Series with the objective of providing a platform for senior officers to share their experiences, professional insights and perspectives on various aspects of leadership, administration and personal effectiveness with the officers and officials of the Department.
The first session of the series was held on 5 November 2026 at the विधायी प्रशिक्षण सभागार, Kartavya Bhavan 2, New Delhi. The session was chaired by Dr. Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, Legislative Department. Smt. Akali V. Konghay, Additional Secretary, Legislative Department, delivered an insightful talk on the theme
“Improving Values and Personal Effectiveness in Leadership”
, sharing her personal experiences and perspectives on the principles of effective leadership.
During the session, Smt. Konghay emphasised that leadership is not confined to positions of authority or formal designations but is reflected in the ability of every individual to influence others through personal conduct, values and actions. She highlighted that leadership begins with personal transformation and requires vision, purpose, effective communication, accountability, collaboration and a commitment to empowering and developing others. She also underscored that leadership is fundamentally rooted in service rather than authority.
Elaborating on the importance of values and purpose in leadership, she introduced the concept of the
‘Five Cs of Purposeful Leadership’
, namely,
Consistency, Culture, Contribution, Community and Curiosity
. She explained that these principles encourage individuals to consciously practise values such as integrity, humility, honesty, compassion and accountability; foster a positive and inspiring organisational culture; recognise and utilise their unique gifts, passions, talents, abilities and resources for meaningful contributions; develop a sense of responsibility towards the larger community; and remain curious, receptive to feedback and committed to continuous learning.
She further emphasised that personal effectiveness goes beyond efficiency in accomplishing tasks and involves becoming a better individual who contributes meaningfully to the lives of others. Highlighting the importance of self-reflection, she encouraged participants to assess their conduct, influence on others and contribution to society. She observed that the true measure of leadership lies in the positive difference one makes in the lives of others and in the ability to inspire and develop future leaders.
The session witnessed the participation of more than 80 officers and officials of the Legislative Department. The interaction provided an opportunity for participants to reflect on the importance of ethical values, purposeful leadership, personal growth and collective responsibility in professional and personal life.
The Interaction Series is envisaged as a continuing initiative of the Legislative Department to promote knowledge-sharing, encourage meaningful interaction and facilitate the sharing of experiences and best practices among officers and officials of the Department.

title: E20 Petrol Supplied by PSU Oil Marketing Companies Meets Prescribed Quality Standards; 893 Samples Across 27 States and UTs Found Compliant
subtitle:
All 56 samples tested in Karnataka also conform to IS 17021 specifications, with ethanol content ranging from 19% to 20%

OMCs seek joint sampling and independent testing under prescribed standards to verify reported ethanol levels in Karnataka
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 NOV 2026 1:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has taken note of the press release issued by the Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, Government of Karnataka, claiming that petrol sold at certain retail outlets in the State contains between 26% and 31% ethanol.
In this regard, the three public sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) — Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) have clarified that the claims, as reported, are not supported by testing conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. E20 petrol supplied by the three OMCs across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline.
They have also raised concerns regarding the sampling procedure and testing methodology adopted for the October 2026 exercise.
Concerns over Sampling and Testing Methodology
The Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024, prescribes a defined procedure for sampling, retention, testing and communication of results.
The prescribed procedure requires six one-litre samples to be drawn, with two samples handed over to the dealer against acknowledgement, two retained by the oil company or department, and two sent to a laboratory specified under Schedule III of the Control Order or notified in the Official Gazette. The sample labels are required to be jointly signed, and the test results communicated to the dealer and the oil company within the prescribed timeframe.
While samples drawn during the September 2026 exercise were routed through the State Level Coordinator to designated OMC laboratories and tested for the quality parameters requested under the MDG 2024, the subsequent exercise in October reportedly involved samples drawn without the participation of OMC representatives. The OMCs have also not received the corresponding retention samples, complete outlet-wise details or laboratory reports, despite seeking these through the State Level Coordinator.
The OMCs have further stated that the reported findings rely on certificates issued by a third-party laboratory rather than testing conducted at a laboratory specified under the Control Order. The certificates do not provide the complete technical details necessary to independently verify the reported ethanol content. The absence of counterpart samples and the prescribed documentation has also denied the OMCs and concerned dealers an opportunity to seek verification or retesting.
Testing Methodology Must Conform to IS 17021
A preliminary technical assessment by the OMCs has also highlighted concerns regarding the ethanol testing methodology cited in the certificates.
Under IS 17021:2018 (Amendment No. 3, August 2025), ethanol content in E20 fuel is required to be determined through prescribed methods, namely Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) under ASTM D5845, water extraction under Annex C, or Gas Chromatography under ASTM D4815/D6839.
Importantly, when Gas Chromatography is used under ASTM D4815/D6839, the sample must first be diluted in a 1:1 ratio with oxygenate-free petrol, and the result corrected against an E10 certified reference material.
However, the certificates cited in the Karnataka press release merely mention “Ethanol % by Gas Chromatography”, without specifying the applicable standard test method, the prescribed dilution procedure or the reference material used for correction. In the absence of these essential details, the reported ethanol figures of 26–31% cannot be independently validated against the methodology prescribed under IS 17021.
The reported density readings also warrant examination. The certificates indicate densities ranging from 0.742 to 0.749 g/cc for samples claimed to contain 26–31% ethanol. This is lower than the 0.752–0.760 g/cc recorded for E20 samples tested by the OMCs under the QCC-1 and QCC-2 surveys. Given that ethanol has a higher density than petrol, a higher ethanol proportion would ordinarily be expected to increase the density of the blend. This discrepancy further underscores the need for testing through the prescribed methodology and verification against appropriate reference samples.
OMC and CHT Quality Monitoring Confirms Compliance
The Centre for High Technology (CHT), under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, has been continuously monitoring ethanol blending and fuel quality across OMC retail outlets.
As part of the OMC/CHT Quality Coordination Cell (QCC) exercise, 893 E20 samples drawn from IOCL (330), BPCL (280) and HPCL (283) depots and retail outlets across 27 States and Union Territories have been tested for ethanol content as per IS 17021, Annex C, at refinery and OMC quality-control laboratories. All 893 samples were found within the prescribed ethanol content range of 19–21%.
Significantly, all 56 samples tested in Karnataka, comprising samples from different locations and all three OMCs, also conformed to the prescribed specifications, recording ethanol content between 19% and 20%, with an average of 19.30%.
These results demonstrate that ethanol blending at OMC retail outlets is monitored and controlled within the prescribed specifications. The findings are inconsistent with the substantially higher ethanol levels reported in the Karnataka press release and reinforce the need for a transparent, technically sound and jointly verifiable testing exercise.
Ethanol Blending is a Controlled and Automated Process
Ethanol blending at OMC refineries and depots is undertaken through established, calibrated and controlled systems. The process involves automatic calibration and proportioning arrangements at the refinery and depot levels, with blending governed by prescribed specifications and quality-control protocols. It is not a manual or arbitrary process of adding ethanol to petrol.
The OMCs maintain established quality-assurance systems across their supply and distribution networks to ensure that the blended fuel meets the applicable BIS specifications before it reaches consumers.
Consumer Impact Claims Require Scientific Assessment
The claims of an estimated annual consumer mileage loss of approximately ₹62,000 crore and vehicle-repair costs of approximately ₹39,000 crore, aggregating to around ₹1.01 lakh crore, also require careful examination against established technical evidence.
More than 30 crore two-wheelers and 4 crore four-wheelers have been running on E20 fuel for over three years. Every day, over 6 crore people visit petrol pumps to refuel their vehicles. If there were a widespread issue with E20 fuel quality, it would be expected to manifest in vehicle breakdowns across this large vehicle base. No such widespread incidence has been reported. This extensive, real-world usage is an important consideration in assessing claims relating to fuel quality and vehicle performance.
The performance and mileage implications of E20 have been examined by the Inter-Ministerial Committee and through studies involving Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM).
As outlined by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas in its response titled “Response to Concerns on Blending of Ethanol in Petrol and Beyond”, published by the Press Information Bureau on August 12, 2025, vehicles calibrated for E20 can experience a mileage reduction of approximately 1–2%, while certain other vehicles may experience reductions of approximately 3–6%, depending on vehicle category and calibration.
Accordingly, applying a blanket assumption of 10% mileage loss across the entire vehicle population and extrapolating it into a national consumer-loss figure of ₹62,000 crore does not constitute a scientifically established assessment. Similarly, the ₹39,000 crore vehicle-repair estimate needs to be substantiated through a transparent assessment of actual vehicle-performance data, materials compatibility studies and documented repair costs.
Concerns relating to materials compatibility and vehicle performance have already been examined through studies involving technical agencies and the automobile industry. Any assessment of the programme's impact must therefore take into account vehicle category, manufacturing specifications, fuel compatibility and the findings of these technical studies, rather than relying on blanket assumptions.
Ethanol Blending Programme Delivers Wider Economic and Environmental Benefits
India's ethanol-blending journey spans more than two decades, beginning with the pilot programme in 2001 and progressing through successive policy interventions, including the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018, and the NITI Aayog Roadmap for Ethanol Blending in India by 2025, prepared in consultation with stakeholders.
The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme is an important component of India's efforts to reduce dependence on imported crude oil, strengthen domestic agricultural value chains and advance energy security.
Ethanol blending programme, since ESY 2014-15, has resulted in:
Foreign-exchange savings of more than ₹1.97 lakh crore.
Substitution of approximately 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil.
Reduction of approximately 952 lakh metric tonnes of CO₂ emissions.
Transfer of more than ₹1.66 lakh crore to farmers.
These measurable outcomes underline the wider economic, environmental and agricultural benefits of the programme, which cannot be assessed solely through a selective comparison of OMC profitability and alleged consumer costs.
During ESY 2025-26 ending 31st October 2026, PSU OMCs procured 1,089 crore litres of ethanol and blended 1,134 crore litres against petrol sales of approximately 5,673 crore litres, in pursuit of the national 20% blending target. The programme operates within a defined national framework, with blending levels and quality parameters monitored across the supply chain. Isolated and unverified allegations of substantially higher or lower blending at individual locations do not provide a meaningful assessment of the programme's overall performance.
The suggestion that OMCs have a commercial incentive to undertake blending beyond the prescribed target is also misplaced. Ethanol procurement involves a significant cost, and every additional litre blended beyond the prescribed proportion would add to the OMCs' procurement costs. The OMCs have no commercial rationale to undertake arbitrary or excess blending.
OMCs Seek Transparency and Independent Verification
In view of the concerns raised, the three OMCs have requested the Government of Karnataka to share the complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the test methodology adopted for the reported findings. They have also sought access to the counterpart samples for independent testing at an authorised laboratory using the prescribed referee method, in the presence of representatives of the State Government and OMCs.
The OMCs remain committed to cooperating with the State Government and other competent authorities in conducting joint sampling and testing in accordance with the Control Order and the MDG 2024. Any deviation established through the prescribed procedure will be dealt with in accordance with the applicable guidelines.
The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas reiterates its commitment to ensuring the quality of petroleum products supplied to consumers, regulatory compliance and consumer protection, supported by established quality-assurance and monitoring mechanisms across the nationwide supply and distribution networks of OMCs.

title: India-EU conclude negotiations to join Horizon Europe programme
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 NOV 2026 11:26AM by PIB Delhi
content:
India and the European Union (EU) have successfully completed negotiations for India’s association with Horizon Europe, the EU’s flagship research and innovation programme. The association of India with the programme marks a strategic move into a long-term institutional framework of research cooperation between both sides, building on existing R&D projects and cooperation under the India–EU Agreement on Science and Technology Cooperation and the India-EU Trade and Technology Council.
The association will facilitate Indian researchers, institutions and industry to participate in the calls for funding under the Programme through collaborative research projects, and have access to European consortia and cutting-edge research infrastructure. It will also deepen talent mobility and lead to co-development of critical technologies, standards and solutions at scale.
The thematic clusters of Pillar II of Horizon Europe, which include health, digital technologies, industry and space, climate, energy and mobility, food and the bioeconomy, align closely with India's research priorities and can build on its scientific strengths. The association adds a significant value to the innovation ecosystem of the country as it marches towards Viksit Bharat 2047.
An exploration of the possible association was launched after the historic India-EU Summit on January 27, 2026, and formal negotiations were initiated as an outcome of the ministerial meeting of the Trade and Technology Council held in Brussels on July 15, 2026.

title: India’s Chemicals and Petrochemicals Sector: A Foundation for Industrial Growth
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 NOV 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s chemicals and petrochemicals industry is expanding its manufacturing base, investment potential and international engagement. Dedicated industrial parks and integrated infrastructure aim to improve production capacity and attract investment. Research funding, specialised institutions and skill development are building expertise for advanced applications. Quality standards and workplace safety measures reinforce responsible industrial practices. Together, these efforts position the sector to pursue greater value addition, technological capability and a stronger role in global chemical markets.
An Industry of Strategic Importance
India’s chemicals and petrochemicals industry is an important pillar of manufacturing, agriculture and industrial development. Its products serve diverse sectors, including pharmaceuticals, textiles, construction, automobiles, electronics and consumer goods. India is the
sixth-largest producer of chemicals
in the world and the fourth-largest in Asia. The sector is currently valued at around USD 220 billion. It is projected to reach USD 300 billion by 2030 and USD 1 trillion by 2040.
India also holds prominent positions in specialised chemical segments. It is the
second-largest manufacturer and exporter of dyes
and
3rd largest exporter of agrochemicals
globally. There are approximately 13,000 large-scale units and 4.45 lakh micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the sector. Several initiatives are advancing chemical manufacturing, research and industrial infrastructure. These include dedicated chemical parks, funding opportunities and measures promoting quality and investment. Together, these efforts seek to strengthen India’s participation in global value chains.
India Chem 2026: Connecting Industry, Investment and Global Markets
The 14th India Chem 2026 was organised from 22 to 24 October 2026 in Mumbai. The three-day event sought to attract investment and promote sustainable growth in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector. Its theme, “
Advantage Bharat: An Emerging Global Chemicals Hub
,” highlighted India’s industrial capabilities and opportunities for international collaboration. With a footfall exceeding 5,000 visitors, the event brought together industry leaders and businesses through country forums, the CEO Forum and sector-specific roundtables. The exhibition showcased technologies, equipment and investment opportunities, while the inaugural India Chem Youth Innovation Challenge encouraged students to develop practical, research-based solutions.
Strengthening Manufacturing Capacity and Industrial Infrastructure
Strengthening domestic manufacturing requires investment, industrial infrastructure and an enabling policy environment. India permits 100% FDI through the automatic route for most chemical sectors. Under the Automatic Route, investment by a person resident outside India does not require prior approval from the government. FDI inflows reached
₹1,04,895 crore
during
2014–2026
, more than double the ₹45,240 crore recorded during 2004–2014.
The production of major chemicals and petrochemicals increased from 45,638 thousand metric tonnes (MT) in 2015–16 to
58,617 thousand MT
in 2024–25. This momentum complements initiatives to expand industrial capacity, develop specialised manufacturing hubs and enhance infrastructure across the sector.
Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions
The concept of Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions (PCPIRs) is to promote the sector in an integrated manner. PCPIR is a specifically delineated investment region having an area of about
250 sq. km
with around 40% of the area earmarked for processing activities. PCPIRs follow a
cluster-based
approach with common infrastructure, basic utilities and support services. These include roads, rail networks, ports, Common Effluent Treatment Plants, sewage disposal plants, water supply and steam generation units. This infrastructure provides a competitive environment conducive to setting up businesses.
India has three operational PCPIRs: Dahej in Gujarat, Visakhapatnam–Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh, and Paradeep in Odisha.
Together, these regions have attracted ₹3.4 lakh crore in investment.
They have generated 3.7 lakh jobs and facilitated the establishment of over 2,200 chemical manufacturing units.
This shared industrial ecosystem provides a foundation for further investment and value addition.
BHAVYA Rasayan: Dedicated Chemical Parks
The Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA Rasayan) Scheme, approved in July 2026, aims to establish
three dedicated chemical parks
. Each park will cover at least 8 square kilometres (2,000 acres) of land. The Centre will provide grants of up to ₹1,000 crore per park, subject to a minimum contribution of ₹500 crore by the concerned State Government. The scheme has a total financial outlay of
₹3,030 crore
. Of this, ₹3,000 crore is allocated for common infrastructure and basic utilities, while ₹30 crore covers administrative expenditure. It will run for five years, from FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31.
The parks will provide
plug-and-play infrastructure
for the chemical industry, helping improve resource utilisation and reduce logistics costs. It will also foster sustainable industrial development through an environment-friendly ecosystem. This includes centralised facilities such as Common Effluent Treatment Plants, Storage and Disposal Facilities, and hazardous waste management infrastructure. The scheme is expected to attract investment, expand domestic production capacity and strengthen global competitiveness.
Plastic Parks: Strengthening Downstream Processing
The Scheme for Setting up of Plastic Parks supports India’s downstream plastic processing industry. It focuses on increasing polymer (a petrochemical) absorption capacity and value addition in the domestic downstream plastic processing industry. Plastic Parks are industrial zones dedicated to plastic-related businesses and industries. Their objective is to consolidate and synergise the capacities of the plastic processing industry. This promotes investment, production and exports while generating employment. Under the scheme, the government provides grant funding up to 50% of the project cost, subject to a ceiling of Rs.40 crore per project. The remaining project cost is funded by the State Government or its agencies, beneficiary industries, etc.
The parks also encourage environmentally sustainable growth through waste management and recycling initiatives. This makes them an important part of India’s efforts to manage plastic waste and strengthen the chemical industry.
Ten Plastic Parks
have been approved across India, of which 4 have achieved
100%
infrastructure completion, including 3 completed during 2025–26.
Research, Innovation and Skill Development
As chemical applications expand across industries, the need for specialised knowledge and technical expertise continues to grow. Several initiatives are advancing these efforts through sector-specific research, specialised technical education and industry-oriented skill development.
Chemical Promotion and Development Scheme
The Chemical Promotion and Development Scheme (CPDS) facilitates the growth of the chemicals and petrochemicals industry through knowledge creation, dissemination and research promotion. It supports studies, surveys, databases and promotional materials to generate sector-specific knowledge. The scheme also incentivises research and innovation by recognising outstanding contributions to these sectors. It provides
Grants-in-Aid
(General) to organisations, industry associations and other entities for workshops, seminars, studies and related activities.
Since 2016, HIL (India) Limited, a public sector undertaking, has conducted farmer training programmes under CPDS.
The Institute of Pesticide Formulation Technology (IPFT) also began conducting these programmes from 2022–23. They promote the safe and judicious use of pesticides and encourage Integrated Pest Management practices.
These practices aim to minimise pesticide residues in food grains, edible oils, fruits and vegetables. As of August 2026, more than
250 programmes
have benefited over
1 lakh farmers
across the country.
Research, Development and Innovation Scheme
Launched in November 2025, the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme has a corpus of
₹1 lakh crore
to catalyse private-sector investment in research and innovation. It provides long-term financing and refinancing on favourable terms for transformative projects. The scheme aims to accelerate advanced technology adoption, strengthen industrial competitiveness and promote self-reliance in critical and emerging technology areas.
Effective 8 October 2026, Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies became an additional technology area eligible for funding under the scheme. This inclusion will strengthen sectoral research and innovation and facilitate the development of indigenous technologies for advanced industrial applications.
CIPET: Technical Education, Skills and Industry Support
The Central Institute of Petrochemicals Engineering & Technology (CIPET) is a centrally funded technical higher education institution. It undertakes Skill Development, Technology Support, Academic and Research (STAR) activities to advance India’s petrochemical and allied industries. CIPET has expanded through several centres and laboratories. These include the Centre for Skilling and Technical Support (CSTS), Plastic Waste Management Centre (PWMC) and School of Advance Research in Petrochemicals (SARP). Other facilities include the Advance Research School for Technology and Product Simulation (ARSTPS) and Advance Polymer Design and Development Research Laboratory (APDDRL).
CIPET’s network now comprises
51 centres
, including
19 established
since 2014. Three of these centres are dedicated to plastic waste management.
The institute has trained nearly
6.72 lakh
skilled professionals, including over 5.21 lakh during 2014–24. It also completed
8.53 lakh Technology Support Service
assignments during the same period.
Centres of Excellence
Centres of Excellence have been established to advance existing technologies, strengthen research and promote the development of new applications.
18 centres
have filed
85 patents
, published over
600 research papers
and developed
105 new technologies
and products. These achievements demonstrate the role of research institutions in building indigenous capabilities and supporting industrial innovation.
Quality, Safety and Responsible Chemical Use
Quality standards and workplace safety are essential to responsible growth in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector. Regulatory measures help ensure product quality, while targeted training equips industrial workers to handle hazardous chemicals safely.
Quality Control Orders
To protect consumers, promote quality manufacturing and curb substandard imports, Quality Control Orders (QCOs) have been issued. As of August 2026,
37 QCOs
are in force, making specified chemical and petrochemical standards mandatory. These orders require domestic manufacturers and importers to comply with the quality parameters prescribed by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).
Workplace Safety and Hazardous Chemical Management
A nationwide training programme has been launched under the Viksit Bharat@2047 Action Plan for the workforce of
Major Accident Hazardous (MAH) Units
. It focuses on the “Safe Handling of Hazardous Chemicals at the Workplace and Reducing Risk Associated with Hazardous Chemicals”. The programme is designed to cover all 2,393 MAH units over 5 years. Each training programme covers 100 participants from 50 MAH units, with two employees attending from each unit.
As of August 2026,
21 training programmes
have been conducted nationwide. These programmes have been attended by 1,376 industrial units and have trained
2,441 personnel
. The initiative seeks to strengthen workplace preparedness and improve awareness of hazardous chemical management.
Towards an Integrated and Competitive Industry
India’s chemicals and petrochemicals industry spans a wide range of manufacturing activities, industrial applications and downstream products. Its development involves expanding production capacity, establishing specialised industrial facilities and creating an enabling environment for investment. Alongside manufacturing, research initiatives and technical institutions contribute to knowledge development, technology advancement and workforce training. Quality standards and hazardous chemical management address product compliance and workplace safety. India Chem 2026 connected these domestic developments with international participation, industry engagement and opportunities for collaboration. Together, these areas reflect the breadth of efforts shaping the sector’s industrial development and global engagement.

ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals

content:
National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, capped trade margins on MRP of 137 anti-cancer drugs,
based on the recommendations of Expert Committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) under Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
on 17th October, 2026.  The revised prices of these drugs will come into effect from 9th November, 2026.
As on date, 76 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRP for 1225 anti-cancer formulations, covering 121 drugs. Reduction in the MRP have been reported in 1031 formulations of anti-cancer medicines, with 600 brands reporting above 50% reduction and the highest reduction being 96.45%. Further, out of the 137 identified anti-cancer drugs, there are 10-15 drugs which are yet to be launched in India. However, Trade Margin Rationalization (TMR) will be applicable on these drugs also as and when they are launched.
